exposure: isolated doses of formula feeding in hospital
Type of delivery (Caesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
Infants with cow milk allergy (CMA) IgE+
outcome: Development of cow milk allergy (CMA) immunoglobulin E (IgE)+
cohort: 211 infants with CMA IgE+ and a control group of infants without CMA IgE+ matched for age and sex
finding: Formula feeding in the hospital, especially after caesarean delivery, was found to be a risk factor for CMA IgE+, while longer duration of breastfeeding and prematurity were protective factors.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was found to be a risk factor for CMA IgE+ when combined with formula feeding in the hospital.
